clinician.trajectory_summary: A 29-year-old woman presented one month after onset of isolated progressive episodic memory loss, with worsening during emotional distress and no psychiatric symptoms. Neurological exam showed an isolated episodic memory deficit. Neuropsychological testing confirmed severe verbal and visual episodic memory impairment with impaired delayed recall on MMSE (27/30). EEG revealed temporal lobe epileptiform discharges without clinical seizures. Brain MRI showed bilateral temporal lobe hyperintense lesions on FLAIR and T2. CSF analysis demonstrated mild pleocytosis and oligoclonal bands. Serum and CSF were positive for NMDAR-IgG antibodies by cell-based and indirect immunofluorescence assays. Imaging ruled out underlying tumor with normal pelvic US/MRI. Total body PET showed slight hypometabolism in right temporal cortex and cerebellar hemispheres. Successful diagnosis of anti-NMDAR encephalitis was made based on combined clinical, electrophysiological, imaging, CSF, and serological data. Treatment course and outcome were not documented.
